correctness.rationale: Finite Fourier diagonalization has eigenvalues 0 and sqrt(3)exp(±i*pi/6). The exact real circulant row formula is derived from the inverse DFT. For 0<alpha<=1 the generator is irreducible Metzler, hence strict positivity. For 1<alpha<3 the three phases cannot be simultaneously below -exp(ds)/2, so negative intervals do not overlap. Each negative-cosine lobe has exactly one maximizer s=gamma_n-arctan(d); its sign criterion H_n(d)>0 has derivative H_n’=-(gamma_n-arctan(d))<0, giving one sharp critical order and exact ceiling count. The asymptotic follows from B(d)=log(2)/d+O(d) and d~pi(3-alpha)/6. At alpha=3 direct trigonometry gives cyclic permutation times. The included independent SciPy exponential check passed 1422 supplementary finite assertions; none are used to infer infinitary completeness.

value.rationale: The exact number of alternating signed-time windows and their ordered critical fractional orders expose a stability boundary invisible to qualitative eventual positivity: after first recovery, a diagonal component can re-enter negativity at the sharp order 2.57023..., then successive cyclic components do likewise infinitely often as alpha tends to 3. The count grows as 1/(3-alpha), the final recovery time has a separate sharp asymptotic constant, and the alpha=3 endpoint gives only isolated permutation times. This is a natural complete time-sign classification of the smallest nonreversible directed network and a finite-dimensional benchmark for loss and recovery of positivity in higher-order fractional transport.
